newsitem.title: USA: American pilots board talks resume, vote expected.
newsitem.headline: American pilots board talks resume, vote expected.

text.p: Board members of American Airlines pilots union will resume meetings Friday morning and are expected to vote on a labor contract proposed by the nation's second largest carrier.
"We will open with a resolution on the floor and then open for debate," said James Sovich, president of the Allied Pilots Association, which represents about 9,300 American Airlines pilots.
"There is a resolution on the floor - 'be it so resolved that the proposal be accepted by the board and sent to APA members for a vote'," Sovich said.
"I see a vote no later than 11 AM," he told a news conference late Thursday in the Chicago suburb of Arlington Heights where the meetings of the union's 18-member board are being held.

"The board is trying to be as responsible as possible. They are trying to be realistic enough to understand that Congressional intervention is a possibility (if the proposed contract is rejected by the board)," he said.

Meetings held all day Thursday were recessed without a vote. The issue of who will fly smaller jets at American Airlines' regional carrier, American Eagle, remained at the center of the meetings on Thursday.
American Airlines pilots are concerned they might lose routes to American Eagle if American Airlines buys new smaller jets for the regional subsidiary.
The pilots had reached an agreement in principle with American last week, although the issue of who will fly small jets at the American Eagle regional division has yet to be settled.

American Airlines wants American Eagle pilots, who are paid less than APA members, to fly smaller jets so the company can remain competitive with low-cost commuter carriers. The APA pilots, however, are concerned that American Eagle pilots will eventually take over their current routes.
Under a proposed five-year deal, American pilots would receive pay increases of 9 percent and options on 5.75 million shares of AMR common stock at $10 below market price.

American Airlines also would be able to add 50- and 70-seat commuter jets at American Eagle, but the APA in return would win a guarantee that any furloughed American pilots would be moved to fly the regional commuter jets.
If the board approves the contract proposal, it would allow for a ratification vote by the rank-and-file. If the board rejects the proposal, another 30-day cooling off period would be launched.
American Airlines is a subsidiary of AMR Corp.
